claims.claim: The requested cabinet, part names, joint, and place target are present; the cabinet body matches the approximate requested size.
claims.evidence: asset/model.urdf: robot drawer_cabinet; root carcass; drawer and fixed child handle; drawer_slide prismatic +X, limits 0 to 0.24 m. asset/asset.json annotations map drawer_opening to tray_floor and the handle to handle_neck. probes/02_geometry.out: carcass bounds [-0.15,-0.21,0] to [0.15,0.21,0.25], four 22 mm legs. Overall depth including the projecting handle is 0.37 m (readings.json size_cm), versus 0.30 m for the body; this is consistent with the separately required projecting handle. renders/front.png, side.png, top.png and iso.png show one drawer facing +X.

claims.claim: The drawer is an open tray meeting the required interior dimensions, with clearance from the carcass.
claims.evidence: readings.json collision_boxes and probes/02_geometry.out: interior X/Y/depth = 0.252/0.356/0.160 m, exceeding 0.25/0.35/0.08 m. Floor, back, two sides and front are present. Closed minimum back/side/top/bottom gaps are 5/4/2/2 mm. No collision box fills the interior or carcass front opening.

claims.claim: Collision geometry follows the visual model and preserves the accessible cavities.
claims.evidence: All four renders, asset/model.py, compiled OBJ meshes and probes/02_geometry.out: all 16 collision boxes have matching mesh extents within 1e-6 m; zero vertices outside their link collision-box union (carcass 1944 vertices, drawer 1080, handle 775). Meshes use beveled panels and a spherical knob; their bounding-box collision approximations preserve the tray cavity and neck access.

claims.claim: The drawer traverses its declared range without interpenetration and remains held by the carcass.
claims.evidence: probes/01_operation.out: no overlaps greater than 0.1 mm at q=0,0.03,0.06,0.09,0.12,0.15,0.18,0.21,0.24 m, or after dynamic operations. Closed/open settled q=0.000129764/0.239870325 m; transient servo overshoot approximately 0.356 mm. probes/02_geometry.out: full-open drawer rear X=0.113 m versus carcass front X=0.150 m leaves 37 mm overlap. Motion is purely +X, preserving lateral and vertical clearances throughout and increasing back clearance. A 20 N downward load for 30 frames leaves q=0.239999995 and drawer pose [0.24,0,0] with identity rotation.

claims.claim: The separate handle provides a neck grasp accessible from above and a knob to pull against.
claims.evidence: readings.json handles and probes/02_geometry.out: grasp at [0.165,0,0.136]; neck is 12 mm across and projects 40 mm from front X=0.145 to knob X=0.185. Knob is 35 mm across. A 20 mm-wide finger centered on the grasp occupies X=[0.155,0.175], clearing the cabinet top front at X=0.150 by 5 mm and knob by 10 mm. The 12 mm neck fits within the 80 mm gripper opening. These approach clearances persist or increase during +X travel; handle_mount fixes it to the drawer.

claims.claim: A 4 cm object placed by the scenario rule on drawer_opening rests inside the rim and remains in the tray during closing and reopening.
claims.evidence: probes/01_operation.py and .out: at q=0.24, scenario X=lip_local.x+q/2=0.145+0.12=0.265 m. A 0.04 m cube dropped from Z=0.32 settles at [0.265,0,0.08394], with bottom Z=0.06394 against tray top Z=0.064 and four drawer contacts totaling 0.980 N. Open interior X=[0.123,0.375], Y=[-0.178,0.178] fully contains it. After closing and reopening, cube centers are [0.02479,0,0.08394] and [0.26487,0,0.08397], respectively, remaining on the floor inside the rim.
